title: genkit-ai/genkit — Open-source framework for building agentic apps in JavaScript, Go, Dart, and Python, built and used in production by Google
content:
Genkit is an open-source framework for building full-stack AI-powered applications, built and used in production by Google's Firebase. It provides SDKs for multiple programming languages with varying levels of stability:
- JavaScript/TypeScript: Production-ready with full feature support
- Go: Production-ready with full feature support
- Python (Beta): Wide feature support approaching production-readiness
- Dart (Preview): Early development with core functionality
It offers a unified interface for integrating AI models from providers like Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and more. Rapidly build and deploy production-ready chatbots, automations, and recommendation systems using streamlined APIs for multimodal content, structured outputs, tool calling, and agentic workflows.
Get started with just a few lines of code:
import { genkit } from 'genkit';
import { googleAI } from '@genkit-ai/google-genai';
const ai = genkit({ plugins: [googleAI()] });
const { text } = await ai.generate({
    model: googleAI.model('gemini-flash-latest'),
    prompt: 'What is the meaning of life?'
});
Play with AI sample apps, with visualizations of the Genkit code that powers them, at no cost to you.
Genkit simplifies AI integration with an open-source SDK and unified APIs that work across various model providers and programming languages. It abstracts away complexity so you can focus on delivering great user experiences.
Some key features offered by Genkit include:
Genkit is designed for server-side deployment in multiple language environments, and also provides seamless client-side integration through dedicated helpers and client SDKs.
- JavaScript/TypeScript quickstart
- Go quickstart
- Python quickstart (Beta)
- Dart quickstart (Preview)
Genkit provides a CLI and a local UI to streamline your AI development workflow.
The Genkit CLI includes commands for running and evaluating your Genkit functions (flows) and collecting telemetry and logs.
- Install: npm install -g genkit-cli
- Run a command, wrapped with telemetry, a interactive developer UI, etc: genkit start -- <command to run your code>
The Genkit developer UI is a local interface for testing, debugging, and iterating on your AI application.
Key features:
- Run: Execute and experiment with Genkit flows, prompts, queries, and more in dedicated playgrounds.
- Inspect: Analyze detailed traces of past executions, including step-by-step breakdowns of complex flows.
- Evaluate: Review the results of evaluations run against your flows, including performance metrics and links to relevant traces.
- Follow us on X/Twitter – Get the latest news, updates, releases, tips and samples from the Genkit team.
- Join us on Reddit – Post questions, learn advanced features, connect with the team and read the latest developments.
- Join us on Discord – Get help, share ideas, and chat with other developers.
- Contribute on GitHub – Report bugs, suggest features, or explore the source code.
- Contribute to Documentation and Samples – Report issues in Genkit's documentation, or contribute to the samples.
Contributions to Genkit are welcome and highly appreciated! See our Contribution Guide to get started.
Genkit is built by Google with contributions from the Open Source Community.

report.summary: Google's open-source Genkit framework enables building AI apps across JavaScript, Go, Python, and Dart with unified multi-provider APIs.
report.background: As large language models proliferate, developers face fragmentation across model providers, programming languages, and SDKs. Google built Genkit internally for Firebase to streamline AI integration into production applications, then released it as an open-source framework. It provides a consistent interface for generating text, structured outputs, tool calls, and agentic workflows while supporting Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and other providers. With SDKs at varying maturity levels—JavaScript and Go production-ready, Python in beta, Dart in preview—Genkit aims to cover both server-side and client-side development. The project also includes a CLI and a local developer UI for running flows, inspecting traces, and evaluating performance, making it a full-stack solution for building and debugging AI applications.
key_points: Multi-language, production-grade support: Genkit offers SDKs for JavaScript/TypeScript and Go that are production-ready, with Python in beta and Dart in preview. This lets teams adopt the framework in their existing backend environments without forcing a language change, while the maturity levels set clear expectations for production use.

Unified model access: Developers write once and run against multiple AI providers, including Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama. This abstraction reduces vendor lock-in and makes it easy to switch or compare models for a given task, using consistent APIs for text, structured outputs, and tool calling.

Built for production at Google: Genkit is used in production by Google's Firebase team. That means it has been tested against real-world scale and reliability requirements, and the open-source release includes tooling for telemetry, tracing, and evaluation—essential for operating AI apps in production.

Strong developer workflow: The Genkit CLI and local UI provide a playground for experimenting with prompts, inspecting step-by-step execution traces, and evaluating flow performance. This integrated workflow helps developers debug complex agentic behavior more easily than with standalone model SDKs.

Easy to start: A minimal setup requires only a few lines of code—import genkit, add a provider plugin, and call ai.generate() with a model and prompt. Each language has a quickstart, lowering the barrier for newcomers to build and deploy AI features.
report.impact: Genkit signals that Google is investing heavily in open-source, multi-provider AI development tooling rather than pushing exclusive dependence on its own models. By standardizing telemetry, evaluation, and agentic workflows in a single framework, it gives developers a robust alternative to vendor-specific SDKs and general-purpose orchestration tools like LangChain. For the broader AI industry, this could accelerate adoption of portable, observable agentic applications. Developers gain flexible, production-ready abstractions that work across languages and providers, while regular users benefit from more reliable and securely built AI-powered features. As Genkit matures in Python and Dart, its influence will likely grow across mobile and cross-platform app development.
report.tools: To explore Genkit, start with the npm package `genkit` and the CLI (`npm install -g genkit-cli`), along with provider plugins like `@genkit-ai/google-genai`. The GitHub repo genkit-ai/genkit provides docs, quickstarts, and sample apps. For comparison, watch LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Vercel AI SDK, which offer similar multi-provider abstractions. If you want to contribute, the project welcomes bug reports, feature suggestions, and documentation improvements.
